evidence: Read the full diff. The new guard on run-ours.sh line 19 runs `jq -e '.rows | type == "array"' "$rows_file"` with output suppressed. It sits after the case lookup and before the per-row `unknown row` loop.
A missing file, malformed JSON, or a non-array `.rows` makes jq exit non-zero. The script then prints `cannot read the rows of <file>` and exits 2. This resolves part (b).
The guard cannot reject valid input. A valid rows file has an array under `.rows`, which is the shape the existing loop already indexes with `.rows[]`.
The default ROWS_FILE path and the `${ROWS:-default,hunt}` default are unchanged (grep of ROWS lines 3, 9 and 10). Part (a) was reported as not reproducing, so no further change was needed.
The new test sets ROWS_FILE to a nonexistent path. It asserts exit 2 and the exact stderr `cannot read the rows of <path>\n`. It matches the guard's output. I did not run the test.
